Excellent food and service
Dec 2015 • Couples
My husband and I stayed at the Coco Beach resort as part of our honeymoon and ate at the onsite Champa restaurant for 2 nights of our stay. As it's the beginning of the tourist season, there were not many people in but this did not take anything away from the atmosphere and the view overlooking the pool.
The flavours and food are amazing throughout the 3 courses and you can really tell there is a French influence. We both had the 'special of the day' 3 course menu on both nights (different courses both nights too) which includes a glass of wine. The highlight was the Tuna carpaccio with pistou which worked so well together to bring out the flavours and exceed our expectations from reading the menu. The lamb and pork we had over the 2 days were cooked perfectly. Desserts are not a strong point in Vietnam, so we were very happy to taste some exceptional dishes, especially the warm apple pastry.
Our waitress was lovely and the service was good too. The only reason we did not go on the 3rd night is because it is closed on a Monday so we had no choice!

Why didn't we pay heed that the restaurant was empty?
Mar 2012 • Family
Deluded by memories of beautiful food here from being a guest at Coco Beach several years I overlooked that the restaurant was empty. After placing our order I was wide eyed with amazement as my glass of wine was set down in front of me - there would have been room to spare if it had been served in a medicine glass! Remarking to the waitress that my glass was almost empty she replied that the owner had told them that they had to get 6 glasses out a bottle - "but at this rate you'll get 20 I said"! They then po faced brought out a little jug of wine for to me top up my glass.
I had ordered the Lobster Tail on creamed ( or mashed) potato with fresh vegetables, and my son ordered the curried chicken. My lobster tail arrived plated on a large white mound of mashed and cubed ( or large lumps) of potato no veges - and my son's curried chicken was an unappetizing yellowish brown. Where are the vegetables? I inquired - we ran out was the reply. My son wasn't faring much better and after tasting his meal we were both doubtful it was chicken - most likely pork. Bringing this to the kitchen's attention they assured us it was chicken. I asked to speak to the owner or Manager however he was in Saigon I was told so they sent for the Chef ( who took sometime as I learned he actually presides over the beachfront restaurant). Whilst I was waiting I ordered another glass 
(thimble) of wine - again it was a miniscule amount - however not wanting to be the customer from hell I didn't complain.
Chef arrived and firstly went to great pains to assure us it was chicken and explained how the chickens are leaner and tougher to what we are used to, and I take on board he may have been correct. The dark brown color and odd flavor of the curry was due to the kitchen burning the tamarind he said. And why no fresh vegetables with the lobster I asked? he hadn't been told the kitchen had ran out he said - to my suggestion that they just go an buy some I was advised they have to be careful where the vegetables are purchased for the sake of our health. 
I then breached the miserable amount of wine that was poured, yes this is a common problem he has with the staff I was told - I keep telling them about that. Being a lateral thinker I suggest they use a measure - yes that is a good idea I have one on order!!! LOL two large restaurants for more than 10 years and they don't have or can't create a measure for 125mls? 
So crap burnt chicken / pork, no veges with meal as described on the menu and thimble size glasses of wine. The chef was friendly and polite and confided that the problem with the kitchen staff was they had learned bad habits from the previous chef. However no apology, no offer of a complimentary dessert ( they were probably out of them) coffee, thimble of wine or reduced bill - nothing to rectify our unhappy and expensive experience.
Very sad as I have mentioned previously I had good memories of fine food and the charming French restaurant manager when I was a guest here years ago.
t don't remember the total bill however I recall the lobster was around USD$25 which is pretty exy for Vietnam. 
Is this a case of not caring as you probably won't be back?

Beautiful - from start to finish!
Aug 2011
Our family recently visited Champa restaurant for dinner and I must say that we had a completely different experience than the last poster. In fact, I have to wonder if it was meant for an entirely different restaurant.?? We had a beautiful experience - from start to finish! I had grilled vegetables as a starter, beef rossini (beef fillet with foix gras) for my main course, a lovely cabernet sauvignon, and chocolate fondant (nothing short of a chocolate dream) for dessert. Not only was my meal magnificent, the service and the ambience were also quite nice. The staff was friendly, courteous, attentive and timely. Nothing was missing from the entire experience. It is not easy to please everyone, but all eight of us walked away very happy. We will be coming back to Vietnam for the TET holiday and I am already looking forward to returning to Champa.

Should've, could've been a much better experience...
I had been looking forward to having another meal at the ChamPa Restaurant after a nice dining experience there well over a year ago. I had tried going to ChamPa over the summer during our previous visit to Mui Ne, but the whole Coco Beach Resort was closed for the "off" season. The venue is gorgeous, overlooking the mature and beautifully groomed grounds of the original, therefore the oldest, Mui Ne resort
On Christmas evening six of us, and a 2 year old child, arrived early in the evening with out reservations, which wasn't a problem as the there were no other customers. We relaxed a bit on some couches with drinks, while our table was prepared, before we all sat down to order. The service was attentive and our orders came out in a reasonable time but there were some issues with how a couple of our dishes were prepared. My "Lamb Rack" (US$15.42)was overcooked but palatable. Another order, "Beef Romini" ($18.14)also was way overcooked although again palatable and not worth making an issue over. Another friend asked for the freshest fish they had in the kitchen and wasn't happy with the way it tasted. he was very unhappy a few hours later when he became violently ill, which required a couple of days to "run"it's course and for recovery. Not good! 
The rest of the dishes were fine, no complaints. The baby liked the Pumpkin & Sweet Potato soup ($2.72). 
The worst part of the evening, for most of us, was that somehow the sparkling wine we had ordered was upgraded to a pedestrian, although pricy, French Champagne, listed at about $50 more than the bottle we had ordered. The manager, Sebastian, was remarkably unsympathetic to the situation, so much so that I had the definite impression that the wait staff are given a bonus for selling the more expensive bottle. Never have I been in a hospitality situation where the customer was so wrong, with absolutely no offer in mediation or mitigation. They just didn't care! If we didn't have the child with us we might have just only paid for what we had ordered and walked!
Our bill totaled $158.50, with the $75 bottle of wine. 
Looking at the receipt now, they might have inadvertently overlooked charging us for a couple of our early drinks while we were waiting to be seated.
While ChamPa strives to be a step above the general level of "resort" cuisine available along the Mui Ne beach, our overall experience was so negative that I can not recommend ChamPa. 
Prior to our disappointing second experience I had been thinking that I would probably be writing a more glowing report. I absolutely can not!
